10.0 CONSTRUCTION PLAN

10.1 Method

V2 is built in nine checkpoints on the version-2 branch. Each checkpoint is a working build that the owner can start on the PC and use, not a progress report. Work stops at each checkpoint for the owner's evaluation; the next begins only on the owner's word, as with V1 phases. V1 stays usable throughout. Each checkpoint ends with its tests passing and the owner's approval, at which point its output becomes the baseline (D-4).

[[FIG roadmap | Checkpoints and their order]]

10.2 Before CP-0: feature lists

For each of the 14 Draw objects, a one-page feature list is drafted from V1: controls, each handle and what it does, infrastructure, and special behaviour (the Multi handle that separates copies; Linked Circles' three link styles; Chords in Ellipse's five modes). The owner corrects them. They record what each object is for, not what it outputs.

10.3 Checkpoints

CP-0   SKELETON
BuiltThe app2/ folder; one Node process serving the page and the requests; Bootstrap, Tab lifecycle, Panels, Library view; Storage (read only) and Catalog reading the existing folders; the call-rule check (FR-6.1.4).
You evaluateStart V2 beside V1. Click through the six tabs. Each category list shows your real patterns, gallery scripts and images by name. Nothing runs yet.
Accepted whenEvery category V1 shows is present; switching tabs leaves nothing behind; the call-rule check passes.
Not yetDrawing, scripts, thumbnails, saving.
CP-1   KERNEL BENCH
BuiltThe kernel (paths, makers, shapers, connectors, finders); the canvas renderer; a Utilities page, the kernel bench, with controls to choose a maker, chain shapers and pick a connector; Node tests for the kernel.
You evaluateMake a circle of 36 points and connect by multiply 2 (a cardioid), then by all pairs. Make a rose with parametric, compare even t with even spacing. Add jitter, change the seed, change it back: the same picture returns. Trim, reverse, start at 4.
Accepted whenYou can build each of Figure 8's four pictures on the bench, and the shapers behave as you expect.
Not yetGenerators, handles, documents.
CP-2   GENERATORS AND CONTROLS
BuiltThe generator format and its load check; the settings schema and Controls; handles on the canvas through Interaction; the folder watcher. Generators: Line, Parabola, Circular Parabola Multi, Linked Circles. The Draw tab using them.
You evaluateOpen each object in Draw: sliders, number boxes, reset; drag handles; nudge with arrow keys. Save a copy of parabola.js under a new id with a change: it appears in Draw within two seconds. Edit it in VS Code and save: the open drawing redraws with your settings kept. Break a file on purpose: it shows a badge, the rest load.
Accepted whenThe four objects match their feature lists; adding a generator needs nothing but saving the file.
Not yetUndo, saving, figures.
CP-3   DOCUMENT, COMMANDS AND UNDO
BuiltDocument, Commands and History, Session, Storage writes; the format-2 file; Save, Save As (one form), open; the unsaved indicator; the remaining ten generators.
You evaluateIn Draw, change settings and drag: Ctrl+Z undoes a whole slider movement or drag in one step; Ctrl+Y redoes. Save; undo back past the save and forward again: the indicator follows. Switch tabs and return: history is still there. Open the saved file in VS Code and read it.
Accepted whenAll 14 objects match their feature lists; undo never leaves a wrong picture; saved files contain no derived values.
Not yetLayers, welds, scripts.
CP-4   FIGURES
BuiltThe Figures tab: layers, layer strip, identity colours, transforms, the point table, shared-point welds, attachments, discs, the Evaluator's ordering, break apart, nesting, roles; the commands table for Figures.
You evaluateBuild the hard test figure: two copies of one object; a hidden layer; a deleted layer; a moved and a turned layer; a free disc and an anchored disc; a corner tied within one layer; a weld across two layers; a line attached to a circle. Drag everything. Undo everything. Save, close, reopen. Try to make an attachment loop.
Accepted whenEvery item of the hard test figure behaves, survives save and reopen, and undoes in one step per gesture; the loop is refused with a clear message.
Not yetScripts, output.
CP-5   SCRIPT HOST
BuiltThe isolated frame; the legacy adapter; the recorder; error badges and time limit; reports and thumbnails on first sight; Patterns and Gallery running scripts.
You evaluateRun a dozen of your scripts in any order, including the two that failed after about 100 runs in V1, arcsAndInner, voronoi and an animated one. Leave an animation: it stops. Read a report. Place a recorded script in a figure as a frozen layer.
Accepted whenRun order no longer matters; a broken script cannot affect another; every legacy script is classified as runs, adapted, preview only, or blocked, with a reason, in a migration ledger.
Not yetThe importer.
CP-6   IMPORTER
BuiltThe importer with levels 1 to 3 and the review panel; New script and Import.
You evaluateTake OverlappingStars.js through Level 1 and compare the proposal with the V1 hand adaptation. Adjust ranges, accept, and check the original is kept. Take one simple script through Level 3 and insert it into a figure.
Accepted whenLevel 1 proposals need only small corrections on your test scripts; nothing is ever rewritten without your approval.
Not yetOutput.
CP-7   OUTPUT
BuiltUnits and scale; output preview; SVG; true-scale PDF with scale bar and 100 mm calibration line; nail list; spacing check; tiling if wanted (O-7).
You evaluateSet the scale for a figure. Print the PDF at actual size on your printer and measure the calibration line with a ruler. Check the nail list against the drawing. Set a nail diameter and see close pairs highlighted.
Accepted whenThe printed 100 mm line measures 100 mm; a weld group prints as one nail; the template is usable on a board.
Not yetHome, Utilities, Help parity.
CP-8   PARITY AND CUT-OVER
BuiltHome with status views; Utilities (tools and lab); Help in Markdown; thumbnails for all items; the parity ledger complete.
You evaluateUse V2 for a week of real work. List anything V1 did that V2 does not.
Accepted whenThe ledger shows every V1 item accounted for and you choose to retire V1.
ThenV2 is merged; app2/ becomes the application; V1's code is removed in a separate, reviewable commit.

11.0 VERIFICATION

FR-11.1Kernel, evaluator, commands, history, schema and storage shall have Node tests that run in seconds without a browser.
FR-11.2Tests shall check meaning before pictures: path lengths, stitch end points, bounds, attachment positions, weld coincidence, undo restoring every partner.
FR-11.3Each generator shall have, once the owner approves it, stored reference geometry and a reference picture. Later changes shall be compared with these; a deliberate change updates them.
FR-11.4A browser test shall cover each screen's wiring and each checkpoint's evaluation steps that can be automated.
FR-11.5Script tests shall run scripts in random order to prove run order no longer matters.
FR-11.6Tests that save shall use a scratch copy, never the owner's library (V1's SKETCHPAD_ROOT rule kept).
FR-11.7Physical output shall be accepted only by a measured print (CP-7).

12.2 From the other evaluations: worth your attention

Four evaluations were considered (R-5, R-6, R-7, and the staged rethink R-4). Most of their substance is in this specification. These items are not, or are only in part, and are worth a look.

SourceItemWhy it mattersStatus here
R-7The physical acceptance test: print at actual size and measure a calibration line.The only real proof a template is right; a screen preview cannot prove it.Adopted (CP-7). Look at R-7 p. 12.
R-7The hard test figure and the migration ledger.A single pretty shape exercises nothing; the ledger accounts for all 185 scripts.Adopted (CP-4, CP-5).
R-7Snap versus attach: snapping aligns once; attaching persists.Both are useful and easy to confuse; the difference should be visible.Partly. Attach is specified; a one-time snap is worth deciding.
R-7Deterministic results and residual-error reporting.Identical edits must give identical results. With ordered evaluation this is natural; reporting where an attachment could not be placed matters.Adopted in FR-6.5.9.
R-7Browser storage, crash recovery, revision conflicts, touch authoring, portable bundles.Valuable for authoring on many devices.Set aside by D-2 (iPad for review only). Revisit only if that changes.
R-6Output engines beyond PDF: plotter (HPGL), laser or vinyl cutter, CNC drilling, DXF for CAD.A plotter could draw stitch lines; a CNC router could drill the holes. Each engine is one file once geometry is data.Worth a look. Not specified; add any you would use (R-6 section 10).
R-6Type checking without a build: // @ts-check and JSDoc comments, so VS Code underlines wrong property names as you type.Catches the misspelled-field class of error; files stay plain JavaScript.Worth a look. Optional under A-2.
R-6One Node process serving both the page and the requests.One window, one port, one command.Adopted in CP-0.
R-63D string art (cylinders, spheres, tubes) as a later phase.Linked Circles already suggests tubes and rings; purpose 2.Not specified. A separate project if wanted.
R-4Staged evolution of V1 instead of a rebuild.Lower risk, nothing stops working.Superseded by D-1. R-6's step table remains a fallback route.
R-8October items deferred then: blend modes (L1), background as a layer (L2, N14), hover information (B20), a context bar (O1), node metadata (L9).Some fit naturally now: background is the image role; node metadata is a field on a point-table entry.Worth a look before CP-4.

13.0 GLOSSARY

AttachmentA point-table entry that lies on another layer's path; one-way.
CatalogThe index of library items, worked out from the folders.
CheckpointA working build the owner evaluates before work continues.
CommandA named change to a document; the only way a document changes.
ConnectorA kernel rule joining path points into stitches.
DiscA numbered point placed on a layer: free, or anchored to a path (an attachment).
DocumentPlain JSON describing a drawing or figure; saved; undoable.
FinderA kernel rule naming points on a path by feature.
GeneratorOne file describing one drawable object or script: meta, settings schema, build or run.
HandleA draggable setting of type point; it names a point in the point table.
KernelThe geometry code: values in, values out, no state, no painting.
MakerA kernel rule producing a path: line, circle, parametric curve and so on.
PanelA side area of the page. Replaces one meaning of V1's "overlay".
PathAn ordered array of points, open or closed.
Point tableThe document's list of numbered points; welds are shared entries.
RendererThe only code that paints: canvas, SVG, PDF, nail list.
SessionView state: selection, mode, zoom. Not saved, not undone.
ShaperA kernel rule turning a path into another path.
WeldTwo handles naming one point (shared), or a handle attached to a path.
